rationale: Both candidates independently converge on the two substantive threads implied by ground truth (the over-broad `!= "cpu"` gating vs. the author's stated cuda/musa-only intent, and the missing/removed test-file coverage), and both correctly catch the FL2VA/Ref2VA copy-paste bug in the recipe — but neither surfaces the reviewer's actual suggested fix (`current_omni_platform.device`) or matches the resolution (dropping the UT rather than adding one), capping recall for both. X edges ahead on precision/actionability: its fork_rng `device_type` analysis is a deeper, source-quoted, higher-severity catch presented as its own headline blocking issue with a one-line fix, plus it adds a novel, correct finding (device_module cached at construction time, unpicklable, breaks an existing test) that Y never raises; Y bundles the same device_type remediation as a footnote inside a broader finding and is otherwise very well evidence-cited but slightly less prioritized/actionable in structure. X's 'empirical' shell trace with redacted output is a minor unverifiable flourish, keeping its precision from being clearly higher despite the stronger technical content.
